name: Moksy
description: Journeys, reviewer/customer/staff roles, MXP/MOX, patterns, reports, the 1:99 goal.

groups.journey: Moksy journey stage, role or term

cards.subject: A Moksy project
says: holds one idea and its document
is created by a customer to start working on an idea
is the container that the interview, the document and the review all belong to
cards.use: want to know where one idea and its document live
not: is created by a reviewer when claiming a job

cards.subject: The Moksy interview
says: has an AI ask the customer a series of questions
turns the customer's idea into answers
supplies the input that the output document is built from
cards.use: need the stage that gathers the customer's answers
not: is carried out by a human reviewer reading the idea aloud

cards.subject: The output document
says: is built from the customer's interview answers
is called report, plan, spec, solution plan, document and blueprint in different parts of the customer interface
is the centre of the product
cards.use: need the thing a customer receives after the interview
not: is written by hand by staff before the interview starts

cards.subject: Expert review
says: comes after the output document is generated
has a reviewer check the document and correct what is wrong
sits between the document and the build stage
cards.use: need the step where a person checks the generated document
not: happens before the customer answers any question

cards.subject: The build stage
says: covers downloads, exports and hiring
comes after expert review
is where the customer takes the result away
cards.use: want to export the document or hire people to build the plan
not: is the stage in which the AI asks its questions

cards.subject: A Moksy customer
says: creates projects and receives documents
starts the journey by typing in an idea
lands on the screen called Home

cards.subject: A Moksy reviewer
says: checks documents and earns from doing so
works from a home area separate from the customer home
is paid for reviews in MOX
not: receives output documents as a customer

cards.subject: A staff operator
says: runs the platform from an operator console
uses the home called the Console

cards.subject: The Console
says: is the staff home in the Moksy lexicon
is the operator console used to run the platform

cards.subject: Home
says: is the lexicon's name for the customer home screen
is where a customer starts in the customer area

cards.subject: An account manager
says: is a person assigned to look after accounts
has no assignment field in code yet according to the fact base
makes the promise of a personal account manager a plan rather than a stored row
cards.use: are asked whether every customer already has a personal account manager
not: is stored as a field on every user record today

cards.subject: A Moksy role
says: is the security ceiling for what a person can do
is independent of the reviewer level
does not change when a user's level is pinned
cards.use: need to explain what controls a person's permissions
not: is calculated from a person's MXP

cards.subject: Level
says: is what someone has earned rather than what they may do
is independent of role
can be frozen by a super admin pin
not: raises a person's security ceiling when it goes up

cards.subject: A real-jobs test run
says: walks one real job post end to end as customer, reviewer, staff and account manager
draws on a pool of two thousand real job posts
earns MXP only, because MOX moves only when real money does
cards.use: test the product against a real job post
not: moves real MOX between wallets in every run

cards.subject: The Moksy lexicon
says: lists the shared words for the product's customer-facing vocabulary
records the six names the output document currently has
notes that MOX and MXP are the two coined words Moksy owns well
not: fixes the stored level numbers to new values

cards.subject: MOX
says: stands for Moksy credit
equals one cent per unit
is held in the Wallet
can be bought in packs
cards.use: need the unit used to price and pay for reviews
not: stands for Moksy Experience Points

cards.subject: MXP
says: stands for Moksy Experience Points
is what a person climbs the Ladder with
is a different thing from the credit used to pay reviewers
cards.use: need the unit that measures progression
not: is held in the Wallet and withdrawn as money

cards.subject: The Wallet
says: holds a person's MOX
is the thing the lexicon pairs with MOX
not: is climbed by earning MXP

cards.subject: The Ladder
says: is climbed with MXP
is the thing the lexicon pairs with MXP
not: holds a person's balance of MOX

cards.subject: Starter MOX
says: is granted when someone joins
gives a new user an opening MOX balance

cards.subject: Escrow
says: holds MOX while a review is open
releases the fee once the review is accepted
also releases the fee if the customer's response window closes without a dispute
cards.use: need to explain why a reviewer is not paid the instant they submit
not: pays the reviewer immediately on submission

cards.subject: The Earnings view
says: shows the MOX a reviewer has earned
is kept separate from Payouts in what reviewers see

cards.subject: The Payouts view
says: shows money sent to a bank
is a separate state from Earnings
not: shows MOX earned but not yet withdrawn

cards.subject: Ledger class E
says: is the only class of MOX that can be withdrawn
holds earned MOX
cards.use: need to know which MOX a reviewer can take out as money

cards.subject: Ledger class R
says: receives MOX from operator grants
cannot be withdrawn and can only be spent in the platform

cards.subject: Ledger class P
says: receives MOX when an operator grants it against a purchase
cannot be withdrawn and can only be spent in the platform

cards.subject: The 20-rung reviewer system
says: runs from Novice up to Titan
is the reviewer level system documented in the README today
has 20 rungs
cards.use: need the level system the README documents

cards.subject: Novice
says: is the lowest rung with a score floor of 5
is where the README's 20-rung system starts

cards.subject: Titan
says: is the top rung with a score floor of 100
is where the README's 20-rung system ends

cards.subject: Expert
says: sits at rung 5 with a score floor of 25
is the default threshold for claiming review jobs
has a threshold that admins can configure
cards.use: need to know the default minimum to claim review jobs
not: is the top rung of the system

cards.subject: The level score
says: is a weighted sum of signals added to a base of 5
is clamped between 5 and 100
is computed automatically unless a level is pinned
not: can go below the base of 5

cards.subject: The score signal set
says: bundles earnings in MOX, completed reviews, peer and admin endorsements, customer reviews, network connections and platform activities
contains seven signals
leaves out lifetime spend, which belongs to the customer ladder

cards.subject: A pinned level
says: is set by a super admin
freezes the automatic computation of a user's level
not: changes the user's role to match

cards.subject: The customer ladder
says: classifies customers as guest, free, paid, premium, vip and vvip
is driven by lifetime spend and an admin tag
is separate from the reviewer levels

cards.subject: The lexicon's six-rung names
says: propose Candidate, Contributor, Reviewer, Senior, Principal and Fellow
would show a level as, for example, Senior · Level 9
leave the stored level numbers and MXP thresholds unchanged
cards.use: are asked what the brand direction would change
not: change the MXP thresholds needed for each level

cards.subject: The Candidate rung
says: has applied but not yet passed the Calibration
holds no claim rights of any kind

cards.subject: The Contributor rung
says: has passed the Calibration
has its first three reviews read by a senior reviewer before they reach the customer
may claim Peer Review one Section at a time at Band C1

cards.subject: The Reviewer rung
says: may claim Expert Review as well as Peer Review
may take Section Reviews at Band C2
may hold two Tracks and three pieces of work at once

cards.subject: The Senior rung
says: adds Priority Review and direct invitations
may delegate Sections
may sign off a Blueprint up to Band C3
may hold three Tracks and five pieces of work at once

cards.subject: The Principal rung
says: is by invitation on a record Moksy can point at
may sign off up to Band C4
has no limit on Tracks and may hold eight pieces of work at once
is one of the people who check a Contributor's first three reviews

cards.subject: Band C1
says: describes Simple work

cards.subject: Band C2
says: describes Single-system work

cards.subject: Band C3
says: describes Complex work

cards.subject: Band C4
says: describes Regulated work
is the highest Band a Principal may sign off

cards.subject: Concurrency
says: is what a rung most visibly buys
rises from one piece of work at a time for a Contributor to eight for a Principal
not: can be raised by buying a higher Membership

cards.subject: A rung's limits
says: is not bought by any Membership
is not permission to take a specific job, because the claim gate still checks conflicts, Band and availability
does not lower the standard of review
does not survive an undeclared conflict
cards.use: are asked whether a rung guarantees access to a particular job

cards.subject: The reviewer Queue
says: holds the jobs a reviewer's accreditation, Band and availability allow
shows the scope, window and fee before a job is claimed
lets a reviewer leave a job at no cost
not: pushes jobs onto reviewers who must accept them

cards.subject: Claiming a job
says: starts the clock on the review
is a choice, since leaving a job in the Queue costs nothing

cards.subject: A correction
says: is a specific fix to a part of a Blueprint that is wrong, with the reason
is accepted or pushed back by the customer
builds the reviewer's standing once accepted
not: is a complete rewrite of the Blueprint

cards.subject: Peer Review
says: is the free check for a customer on the free Membership
carries no money and earns MXP
is where a new reviewer builds a record

cards.subject: Expert Review
says: is claimed from the Reviewer rung upward
is a paid review rather than a free check

cards.subject: The Calibration
says: is a blind review of a seeded document with planted defects
takes 45 to 60 minutes
is sat by everybody who applies
cards.use: need the step that proves a reviewer can catch real flaws
not: can be skipped by someone who types a high level into the form

cards.subject: Accreditation
says: is held per Category
lets one reviewer sit on different rungs in different fields
is calibrated rather than granted because someone likes you

cards.subject: Prior experience
says: sets the rung and Band a reviewer starts on
never decides whether a person is asked to sit the Calibration
not: exempts senior applicants from the Calibration

cards.subject: A disputed review
says: goes to a senior reviewer to adjudicate
is settled by a decision that determines whether the review counts as accepted
sends the fee the way the decision goes
not: is settled by the Wallet balance of the customer

cards.subject: A review returned late
says: is declined work with extra steps
earns no payment when returned outside the window the job carries
not: is paid in full if the corrections are good

cards.subject: An acceptable review
says: points at a Section and says what is wrong with it
can be verified by someone else without taking the reviewer's word
is proportionate to the flaw it addresses
is conflict-free and the reviewer's own work
cards.use: are asked what makes a review acceptable at every rung

cards.subject: Disagreeing with a whole Blueprint
says: is argued in the review with reasons rather than asserted
belongs in the review itself, not in a side message
not: is a footnote when the flaw is major

cards.subject: Independence
says: means reviewing the plan in front of you on its merits
forbids softening a review to protect an acceptance rate
lets a reviewer decline at no cost when they cannot be independent

cards.subject: A conflict of interest
says: must be declared before accepting work, not after
can be a commercial relationship with the customer or work for a direct competitor
can be an interest in the tools or suppliers the plan recommends
not: disqualifies a reviewer the moment it is disclosed

cards.subject: Confidentiality
says: covers everything in a customer's plan
continues after the review ends
forbids feeding a plan into a tool that retains it
not: ends when the review is accepted

cards.subject: Competence
says: means accepting only work you can judge
holds that a confident review from outside your domain is worse than none
not: is counted against a reviewer who leaves a job in the Queue

cards.subject: Your own work
says: allows a model to help you read or draft
forbids submitting a model's output as the review
ends the account when passing it off is found

cards.subject: Conduct towards customers
says: asks a reviewer to be direct about what is wrong and civil about who wrote it
holds that contempt is not rigour

cards.subject: A breach of the code
says: is reviewed by a senior reviewer or by Moksy
can end in a correction, a level reduction, suspension or removal
leads to withheld fees only where the work itself was fraudulent
not: always ends in a permanent ban

cards.subject: The API gateway
says: is the only public API entry
listens on port 5001 in the local stack
has a controller that holds nearly ten thousand lines of business logic, which the review flags
not: is reachable only from inside the internal Docker network

cards.subject: The dashboard
says: is the web app people log into
is a Vite app on port 3001 locally

cards.subject: The documentation site
says: is the Docusaurus developer documentation
runs on port 3000 locally

cards.subject: The health endpoint
says: is exposed by every service
lets a deploy check that a rebuilt service came up

cards.subject: The foundation folder
says: holds 25 backend services
sits beside two frontends and three shared packages
not: holds a single monolithic application

cards.subject: The internal Docker network
says: gives the backend services no route to the host
is bridged to the outside only by the gateway

cards.subject: Database per service
says: gives each service its own logical database
was found by the architecture review as 23 distinct databases
means no service reads another's collections
not: puts every service on one shared collection

cards.subject: The service handshake
says: combines a gateway key with a short-lived internal token
is rated amber by the architecture review
relies on one shared secret and plain http between services
not: uses mutual TLS certificates for each service

cards.subject: The events service fan-out
says: delivers events inline over HTTP
happens with no message broker in place

cards.subject: The architecture review verdict
says: puts the platform roughly 60 percent of the way to a proper microservice architecture
rates the service-to-service handshake amber
not: declares the platform fully complete as a microservice system

cards.subject: The moksy-mvp prototype
says: interrogates a sample project with 42 questions
generates a 10-phase solution document
ships with school management, e-commerce and healthcare portal sample datasets
not: is the production microservice platform

cards.subject: The 1:99 goal
says: wants 99 percent of the work done by machine and 1 percent by a human
is the founder's goal in the pattern architecture brief
not: is a pricing ratio between two plans

cards.subject: A Moksy pattern
says: is one smart decision with an id, typed inputs and outputs, bounded parameters and versioned revisions
is the unit that every smart decision in Moksy is meant to be

cards.subject: A flow
says: is a set of patterns and flows with named exports
can itself be used as a step, so patterns combine into bigger patterns

cards.subject: The pattern registry
says: declares 110 patterns, 18 of them implemented
lists 12 flows such as project profile, scope, solution, delivery, document and blueprint
not: shows all 110 patterns as implemented

cards.subject: A selection shape
says: is one of seven ways a pattern decides: classify, cover, configure, retrieve, derive, trigger or attach
returns a because alongside its answer

cards.subject: The because
says: lets a person see and correct a decision
comes back with every selection shape's answer

cards.subject: The decidedBy stamp
says: marks every dispatch as decided by machine or human
is how the 1:99 share is measured rather than guessed
not: is a survey of staff each quarter

cards.subject: The migration status of the live interview
says: was, as written on 2026-09-14, decided inline in a large service file rather than through the dispatcher
meant measured 1:99 coverage was 0 percent
was a brief for founder review
not: showed 99 percent machine decisions on the live path

cards.subject: The traceable-number rule
says: requires every number, name, date and judgement shown to a customer to resolve to a locally held row
requires a pinned version and a source for each fact
not: lets a model supply any figure that sounds plausible

cards.subject: The model-phrasing rule
says: lets a model phrase a figure
never lets a model originate one
not: forbids the model from writing any sentence in a report

cards.subject: The missing-fact behaviour
says: has the system refuse, ask, derive or give a band
avoids inventing a number when a fact is absent
not: fills the gap with the model's best guess

cards.subject: The analysis-area set
says: numbers 22 and is what reports cover
is called pillars internally
is kept out of customer-facing copy, which uses plain wording

cards.subject: The report-type count
says: disagrees between sources, 58 in the lexicon and 57 in the real-jobs brief
has a code catalogue of 37 that is to be amended
cards.use: are asked how many kinds of report Moksy has

cards.subject: The target report
says: names the organisation or person's real problem and the challenges each actor faces
gives who builds it at which level, how long it takes and what it costs in their currency

cards.subject: The solution-option list
says: includes from scratch, rebuild, open source, closed source, a corporate suite or a hybrid
is weighed in the target report alongside the automated version

cards.subject: The Docker-first rule
says: has everything run in Docker
tells developers not to run npm install on the host
avoids platform-specific binaries from the host crashing in containers
not: asks developers to install dependencies on the host first

cards.subject: The quick start
says: copies .env.example to .env and fills the required secrets
then runs npm run dev, followed by npm run seed and npm run seed:personas

cards.subject: The mandatory-secret set
says: numbers seven
includes the JWT secrets, the internal gateway key and the Mongo app credentials
must be set or the services will not boot

cards.subject: Mock billing mode
says: simulates subscriptions and MOX top-ups instantly
is one of two local billing modes

cards.subject: Stripe test mode
says: uses Stripe test keys
charges no real money, as the other local billing mode

cards.subject: The local AI default
says: is a local Ollama model
sets the OPENAI_API_KEY variable to ollama on purpose
not: requires a paid hosted API key to start

cards.subject: Manual deployment
says: happens only when someone pulls on the server
means pushing to GitHub deploys nothing
not: runs automatically on every push to GitHub

cards.subject: npm run deploy:prod
says: rebuilds only the services that changed
health-checks the result and records the commit
has a plan-only preview

cards.subject: A problem statement
says: says who has what problem and why it matters
comes before a solution is proposed

cards.subject: A minimum viable product
says: is the smallest version that tests the core assumption with real users
trades completeness for early learning
not: is a low-quality version never intended to improve

cards.subject: Jobs to be done
says: frames demand as the progress a customer wants to make
looks at the situation a person is in rather than their demographics

cards.subject: A user story
says: describes a need from the user's point of view
is often written as as a user, I want, so that

cards.subject: An acceptance criterion
says: states a testable condition a story must meet
lets the team and the requester agree when work is done

cards.subject: A product roadmap
says: communicates direction and priorities over time
is better framed as outcomes than as a promise of dates

cards.subject: A backlog
says: is an ordered list of work waiting for the team
is reordered as priorities change

cards.subject: Prioritisation
says: weighs expected impact against effort and strategy
decides what not to do as much as what to do

cards.subject: Product discovery
says: tests whether a problem and solution are worth building before committing
uses interviews and prototypes to cut the risk of building the wrong thing

cards.subject: Product-market fit
says: means a real market keeps choosing the product
shows up as retention and demand rather than a launch-day spike
not: is reached the day the first feature ships

cards.subject: Activation rate
says: measures the share of new users who reach a first meaningful action
is an early signal of whether onboarding works

cards.subject: Retention
says: measures how many users keep coming back over time
is usually read as a curve by cohort

cards.subject: Churn rate
says: measures the share of customers who stop over a period
is the loss that retention work tries to reduce

cards.subject: Conversion rate
says: measures the share of visitors who complete a target action such as signing up or paying
is read at a given step of a funnel

cards.subject: Funnel analysis
says: shows how many users drop off at each step of a sequence
points to the step that loses the most people

cards.subject: Cohort analysis
says: groups users by a shared start period to compare behaviour over time
stops a mixed-age user base hiding a trend

cards.subject: A north-star metric
says: is the single measure that best captures the value customers get
aligns teams on one outcome
not: is the same as monthly revenue by definition

cards.subject: Time to value
says: measures how long a new user takes to experience the product's benefit
falls when onboarding removes friction

cards.subject: Customer lifetime value
says: estimates the total revenue or margin a customer brings over the relationship
is read against the cost of winning that customer

cards.subject: A rubric
says: defines criteria and levels for judging work consistently
lets two reviewers apply the same standard

cards.subject: Inter-rater agreement
says: measures how often independent reviewers reach the same judgement
reveals when a standard is too vague to apply consistently

cards.subject: A seeded defect
says: plants a known flaw in a test item to see whether a reviewer catches it
turns a review into a measurable test

cards.subject: A golden set
says: is a set of items with trusted answers used to check quality
can be rerun after a change to see whether quality moved

cards.subject: A sampling audit
says: checks a random sample of finished work rather than all of it
estimates quality across a large volume at lower cost

cards.subject: A blind review
says: hides information that could bias the reviewer, such as the author's identity
keeps judgement on the work itself

cards.subject: The four-eyes principle
says: requires a second person to check work before it is released
reduces the chance that one person's mistake gets through

cards.subject: A regression check
says: re-tests existing behaviour after a change
catches a fix that quietly breaks something that worked

cards.subject: Freemium
says: offers a free plan to attract users and sells upgrades
depends on a share of free users paying later

cards.subject: A free trial
says: gives access for a limited time before payment is required
ends in a choice to subscribe or leave

cards.subject: Usage-based pricing
says: charges according to how much is consumed
needs metering to record consumption

cards.subject: Seat-based pricing
says: charges per user account
grows with the number of people using it

cards.subject: An entitlement
says: defines which features or limits a plan grants
is checked by the product to decide what a customer may do

cards.subject: Metering
says: records consumption so that usage can be billed
must be accurate because invoices depend on it

cards.subject: Proration
says: charges a partial amount when a plan changes mid-cycle
keeps an upgrade fair for the days left

cards.subject: A grace period
says: keeps access for a short time after a payment fails
gives the customer a chance to fix the problem before service stops

cards.subject: A feature flag
says: lets code ship switched off and be enabled later
can disable a feature without a new deploy

cards.subject: A canary release
says: sends a new version to a small share of traffic first
limits the damage if the release is bad

cards.subject: A rollback
says: returns to the previous known good version
is the fastest safe response to a release that breaks things

cards.subject: A service-level agreement
says: states the response or availability a customer can expect
turns a support promise into something measurable

cards.subject: Triage
says: sorts incoming issues by severity and urgency
decides what is handled first

cards.subject: A severity level
says: classifies how serious an incident is by impact
sets how fast and how widely people must respond

qa.q: What does Moksy's tagline promise to turn an idea into?
qa.right: A build-ready plan
qa.why: The tagline is turning an idea into a build-ready plan.

qa.q: How much is one MOX worth?
qa.right: One cent
qa.why: 1 MOX equals one cent.

qa.q: Which unit does a person climb the Ladder with?
qa.right: MXP
qa.why: MXP is Moksy Experience Points, used for the Ladder; the Wallet holds MOX.

qa.q: Which service is the only public API entry in the Moksy platform?
qa.right: The gateway
qa.why: Everything else sits on an internal Docker network with no route to the host.

qa.q: On which port does the gateway listen in the local stack?
qa.why: The gateway is on 5001; the docs site is on 3000 and the dashboard on 3001.

qa.q: In the customer journey, what immediately follows the interview?
qa.right: An output document is generated from the answers
wrong: The customer is charged for hosting
qa.why: Answers become the input to the document; expert review and the build stage come after.

qa.q: Which stage covers downloads, exports and hiring?
qa.right: The build stage
qa.why: The build stage follows expert review.

qa.q: A new developer wants to speed up Moksy's local start by running npm install on the host. What does the README say?
qa.right: Do not; everything runs in Docker, and host installs leave platform-specific binaries that crash in containers
wrong: Do it, because the dashboard needs host node_modules
Do it, but only for the shared packages
qa.why: The Docker-first rule avoids host binaries leaking into containers.

qa.q: Someone pushes a commit to GitHub and expects production to update. What actually happens?
qa.right: Nothing is deployed; deployment is manual with git pull and npm run deploy:prod on the server
wrong: A plan-only preview is posted to the team
qa.why: Pushing to GitHub deploys nothing.

qa.q: A new developer runs the stack but the services refuse to boot. What should be checked first?
qa.right: That the seven mandatory secrets are set in .env
wrong: That npm install was run on the host
That Stripe live keys are present
That the OPENAI_API_KEY holds a paid key
qa.why: Services will not boot without the mandatory secrets copied from .env.example and filled in.

qa.q: Which local billing mode simulates subscriptions and MOX top-ups instantly?
qa.right: Mock
qa.why: Mock simulates; Stripe test mode uses test keys and charges no real money.

qa.q: Which of these does a reviewer see as money sent to a bank?
qa.right: Payouts
qa.why: Earnings show MOX earned; Payouts show money sent to a bank.

qa.q: What is the default threshold for claiming review jobs on the README's 20-rung system?
qa.right: Expert (rung 5)
qa.why: Expert is the default and admins can configure it.

qa.q: A support agent is asked how many reviewer rungs there are. The published Levels page lists five and the internal lexicon six. What should the agent do?
qa.right: Quote the published five and say they will confirm whether a further rung exists
wrong: Say there are six, because the lexicon is more recent
Say there are twenty, from the README
Say the number depends on the Membership
qa.why: Support quotes the published pages and confirms disagreements rather than guessing.

qa.q: A customer asks whether the AI makes up the figures in their report. What is the rule?
qa.right: Every number should resolve to a stored fact with a source, and a model may phrase a figure but never originate one
wrong: The model may estimate any figure it is confident about
Figures are written by the reviewer from memory
Numbers are only shown in the free Membership
qa.why: The traceable-number rule is the centre of the report.

qa.q: A report needs a figure that Moksy holds no fact for. What should the system do?
qa.right: Refuse, ask, derive it or give a band
wrong: Copy the nearest figure from another customer
qa.why: A missing fact is never filled by an invented number.

qa.q: A reviewer's MOX came from an operator grant. Can they withdraw it?
qa.right: No, because only class E, earned MOX, is withdrawable
wrong: Yes, as soon as the grant lands
Yes, if they hold the Expert rung
qa.why: Operator grants go to class R, or to class P against a purchase, and those can only be spent in the platform.

qa.q: A user is promoted from developer to cto and a teammate expects their reviewer level to change too. What happens?
qa.right: Nothing happens to the level, because role and level are independent
wrong: The level rises to match the new role
qa.why: Role is the security ceiling; level is what someone has earned.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT one of the seven signals in the level score?
qa.right: Lifetime spend
qa.why: Lifetime spend drives the customer ladder instead.

qa.q: Between which values is the level score clamped?
qa.right: 5 and 100
qa.why: The score is a weighted sum added to a base of 5 and clamped to 5 to 100.

qa.q: A reviewer notices a customer's plan recommends a tool they hold shares in. What should they do?
qa.right: Declare the conflict before accepting the work, or decline
wrong: Accept and disclose after the review
Review it but avoid commenting on that tool
Ask the customer to remove the tool first
qa.why: Conflicts are declared before work is accepted; concealment, not disclosure, is the offence.

qa.q: A reviewer uses a model to help read a plan, then writes their own corrections. Is that allowed?
qa.right: Yes, because using a model to help read or draft is fine so long as the review is their own judgement
wrong: No, any use of a model ends the account
Yes, even if they submit the model's output unchanged
qa.why: Submitting a model's output as the review is what is forbidden.

qa.q: A Contributor wants to claim a Section Review at Band C2. Will the claim gate allow it?
qa.right: No, a Contributor may claim Peer Review one Section at a time at Band C1
wrong: Yes, as long as they declare their Track
Yes, if their Membership allows it
Yes, with a senior reviewer reading it
qa.why: Section Reviews at C2 begin at the Reviewer rung.

qa.q: Which rung may delegate Sections?
qa.right: Senior
qa.why: Senior adds Priority Review, direct invitations and delegation.

qa.q: Which Band describes regulated work?
qa.right: C4
qa.why: C1 Simple, C2 Single system, C3 Complex, C4 Regulated.

qa.q: A customer disputes a reviewer's work. Who adjudicates?
qa.right: A senior reviewer
wrong: The reviewer's own peers at the same rung
qa.why: Their decision settles whether the review counts as accepted, and the fee follows.

qa.q: Why is a reviewer's fee not paid the instant they submit?
qa.right: It is held in Escrow until the review is accepted or the response window closes without a dispute
wrong: It is held until the next payout cycle
It is held until the reviewer reaches the next rung
It is converted to MXP first
qa.why: Escrow protects both sides while a review is open.

qa.q: What happens when a super admin pins a user to a level?
qa.right: Automatic computation of their level is frozen
wrong: Their level is hidden from them
qa.why: A pin overrides the signal-based score.

qa.q: Which is the best example of an acceptable correction in a review?
qa.right: Section 4's data model contradicts section 2; here is the corrected relationship and why
wrong: Rewrite section 4 entirely in your own words
This is not how I would build it
qa.why: A correction points at a Section, says what is wrong and can be verified by someone else.

qa.q: The founder asks whether Moksy has reached 1:99. What is the honest answer from the pattern brief?
qa.right: No; the live path decides inline rather than through the dispatcher, so measured coverage read 0 percent when the brief was written
wrong: Yes, because 18 of 110 patterns are implemented
Yes, because the brief states the goal
It cannot be measured at all
qa.why: The share is measured by the decidedBy stamp, and the live interview had not been migrated.

qa.q: How is the 1:99 share meant to be measured?
qa.right: By stamping every dispatch decidedBy as machine or human and counting
qa.why: Measured, not guessed.

qa.q: Which is a documented weakness of how the events service sends events?
qa.right: It fans out inline over HTTP with no message broker
wrong: It writes directly into other services' databases
It uses a separate public port
It sends events only on deploy
qa.why: The architecture review flags this.

qa.q: Why did the architecture review rate the service handshake amber?
qa.right: One shared secret, divergent client copies and plain http between services
wrong: It uses no token at all
It requires a human to approve each call
qa.why: A gateway key plus a short-lived internal token is used, but with those weaknesses.

qa.q: A senior engineer with fifteen years of experience asks to skip the Calibration. What is the answer?
qa.right: Everyone sits it; experience sets the rung and Band they start on, not whether they are asked
wrong: Skip it if they hold a Principal role elsewhere
Skip it if they email careers
Skip it only for the free Membership
qa.why: A level typed into a form is not evidence.

qa.q: Why are a new reviewer's first three reviews read by a senior reviewer?
qa.right: To protect the customer while the reviewer's record is short, at no cost to the reviewer
wrong: To charge the reviewer for supervision
To hold the fee until the next rung
qa.why: The check protects the customer; the reviewer does not pay for it.

qa.q: A customer on a sales call is told every Moksy customer has a personal account manager. What should a careful colleague say?
qa.right: That is a plan: no account-manager assignment exists in code yet
wrong: Confirm it, since it is in the lexicon
Say it is available only on premium customers
Say it is handled by the payments service
qa.why: The fact base says the promise is not yet a stored row.

qa.q: Someone asks how many kinds of report Moksy produces. Which answer is most accurate?
qa.right: The sources disagree: 58 in the lexicon and 57 in the real-jobs brief; confirm before quoting
qa.why: The 22 are analysis areas, 110 are patterns, and 37 is a catalogue to be amended.

qa.q: A review comes back after the window the job carried. What is the consequence?
qa.right: It earns no payment, as late work is declined work
wrong: It is paid at half the usual rate
It is paid in full if the corrections are good
It is paid in MXP instead
qa.why: Work returned outside the window is not paid.

qa.q: A new team plans to reward reviewers for their acceptance rate. What risk does the code of conduct point to?
qa.right: Reviewers may soften reviews to protect the rate, which breaks independence
wrong: Reviewers will leave the Queue empty
qa.why: Independence forbids softening a review to protect an acceptance rate.

qa.q: The lexicon's six plain names were adopted. What changes in the product?
qa.right: Only the words people read; stored level numbers and MXP thresholds stay the same
wrong: The MXP thresholds for each level
The roles that can claim jobs
qa.why: The lexicon says only the words change.

qa.q: An operator wants to grant a reviewer MOX that they can withdraw. What does the ledger allow?
qa.right: No path creates withdrawable MOX; whether to open one is a pending founder decision
wrong: A grant to class R that becomes withdrawable after 14 days
A grant to class P that converts on payout
qa.why: Operator grants go to R, or to P against a purchase.

qa.q: What does an experiment run earn?
qa.right: MXP only, because MOX moves only when real money does
qa.why: The real-jobs brief keeps test runs from moving real money.

qa.q: A reviewer disagrees with a whole Blueprint, not just a Section. How should they handle it?
qa.right: Say so in the review with reasons; it has to be argued, not asserted
wrong: Leave a short note in a side message
qa.why: Disagreement belongs in the review itself.

qa.q: A team wants to release a feature to a small share of users first, to limit damage if it is bad. Which practice is this?
qa.right: A canary release
qa.why: A canary sends the new version to a small share of traffic first.

qa.q: Which metric measures the share of new users who reach a first meaningful action?
qa.right: Activation rate
qa.why: Activation is an early signal of whether onboarding works.

qa.q: Churn rises after an onboarding change. What should the team do first?
qa.right: Compare cohorts by signup period before and after the change
wrong: Look only at the overall average
qa.why: Cohort analysis separates a real effect from a mix of older and newer users.

qa.q: A customer upgrades mid-month and is charged only for the remaining days at the higher price. What is this called?
qa.right: Proration
qa.why: Proration charges a partial amount when a plan changes mid-cycle.

qa.q: A team has forty feature requests and capacity for five. What is the sound way to choose?
qa.right: Weigh expected impact against effort and strategy, and decide what not to do
wrong: Build those requested by the loudest customer
qa.why: Prioritisation is a trade-off.

qa.q: Trial users sign up but rarely return after the second day. Which measure most directly points at the cause?
qa.right: Time to value
qa.why: If users do not feel the benefit quickly they leave early.

qa.q: A new release raises the error rate sharply. What is the fastest safe response?
qa.right: Roll back or switch the feature off, then investigate
wrong: Wait to see whether it settles
Ask users to clear their cache
Add logging and keep the release live
qa.why: A rollback or flag returns to a known good state first.

qa.q: Two reviewers score the same item very differently. What does this suggest?
qa.right: Low inter-rater agreement, so the rubric may be too vague to apply consistently
qa.why: Disagreement across raters often traces to unclear criteria.

qa.q: A customer's card payment fails. The product keeps access for a few days while they fix it. Which mechanic is that?
qa.right: A grace period
qa.why: A grace period delays service loss after a failed payment.

qa.q: A support queue holds an outage report and a typo report. How should triage proceed?
qa.right: Rank by severity and impact, so the outage is handled first
wrong: Wait for the typo reporter to escalate
qa.why: Triage sorts by severity and urgency.

qa.q: A founder wants to ship the full plan before talking to any user. What does product discovery advise?
qa.right: Test the problem and solution with users first, to cut the risk of building the wrong thing
wrong: Ship the full plan, then measure
Add more features to reduce risk
qa.why: Discovery precedes commitment.
